A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DPCR research work, with complete, readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Pages 2–14 render identically; page 1 differs only in the arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original DPCR experiments on CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet-100, including component ablations, exemplar-based comparisons in Appendix C, and normalization sensitivity experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original benchmark results, ablations, and experiments in Appendices C and D.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same representation learning, task-wise and category-wise projections, ridge-regression classifier reconstruction, and category-wise normalization procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same class-incremental tasks on CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet-100. Appendix C retains its CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100 coverage; no datasets or test scenarios change.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains LwF, SDC, PASS, ACIL, DS-AL, ADC, and LDC. The analysis comparisons are unchanged, as are Appendix C's iCaRL-CNN, iCaRL-NCM, PODNet, and FOSTER comparisons.

E3.justification: Both retain randomly initialized ResNet-18 models, equal class partitions into 10 or 20 tasks, and final and average incremental accuracy metrics. Training settings, preprocessing, and Appendix C's exemplar budgets of 500 and 1000 are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 retains the component ablations, DP-NCM comparison, stability/plasticity analyses, and decision-boundary visualization. Appendix D retains the same analysis of normalization across ridge-regression regularization values.

E5.justification: Both report means over three class orders: one unshuffled and two shuffled using seeds 1992 and 1993. Appendix C retains seed 1993. No uncertainty estimates or statistical reporting practices change.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted findings in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–7 are identical. For example, Table 1 reports DPCR's CIFAR-100, 10-task final and average incremental accuracies as 50.24% and 63.21% in both versions.

T1.justification: The task definitions, assumptions, projection derivations, and classifier-reconstruction mathematics in Section 3, including Equations 1–22, are identical. No mathematical corrections or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about addressing semantic shift and decision bias, balancing stability and plasticity, and outperforming the evaluated EFCIL methods.

C2.justification: Interpretations of projection effectiveness, classifier balance, and performance against exemplar-based methods are unchanged. Appendix D retains the explanation that normalization provides benefits beyond regularization; no limitations or qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Appendices A and B retain identical pseudocode, augmentation descriptions, optimization schedules, and method-specific hyperparameters. Implementation and resource-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are identical, including the positioning relative to regularization-based, prototype-based, and analytic continual learning. No cited works or novelty comparisons change.

P1.justification: Only the first-page marginal stamp changes from arXiv:2503.05423v1, 7 Mar 2025, to arXiv:2503.05423v2, 8 May 2025. All paper wording, headings, and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7, Tables 1–4, Algorithm 1, captions, and page layout are unchanged. The version/date text update does not alter their presentation or placement.

improvement.justification: The complete scientific content and presentation, including Appendices A–D, are identical apart from the arXiv version/date stamp. This administrative update provides no meaningful improvement or deterioration in evidence, clarity, reproducibility, or overall paper quality.
